statement: PRC FX rules do not restrict current-account international payments and transfers, but current-account FX receipts and payments must rest on a genuine, lawful transaction basis.
Capital-account FX payments require valid documents (and SAFE approval where prescribed) before purchase or payment.

topic: PRC — is there a conversion tax?
statement: No tax levied specifically on exchanging CNY for USD was found in the PRC FX instruments reviewed. This is an absence-of-evidence finding from the documents read, not proof that no other tax can apply to the underlying money.
A per-person annual quota of USD 50,000 equivalent applies to settlement of foreign exchange by all individuals and to purchases of foreign exchange by domestic individuals (境内个人) only.

topic: PRC FX — domestic individual above quota
statement: A domestic individual purchasing foreign exchange above the annual quota for a non-operating current-account purpose must present valid ID plus documents showing the transaction amount.
A foreign individual (境外个人) converting lawful current-account RMB income earned in China must present valid ID and transaction-amount source-of-funds materials, expressly including tax documents.
locator: S02 Art. 13(1); S03 answer quoting Hui Fa [2020] No. 14 Art. 59

topic: PRC FX — foreign individual and the quota
statement: A foreign individual is entitled to the annual facilitation quota for FX purchase only if holding a Foreign Permanent Resident ID card.
PRC rules set no time limit on converting a foreign individual's lawful RMB income, but the bank must be able to verify the original income evidence under due-diligence principles.

The remittance formality may be completed by an authorised other person, including company finance staff, and beyond-quota purchase/settlement and any foreign-individual purchase may be entrusted to others with the prescribed documents.

Unspent RMB from an earlier FX conversion may be converted back with the original exchange memo within 24 months; same-day amounts up to USD 500 (or USD 1,000 at port facilities before departure) can be handled on ID alone.

Outward transfer of assets by an individual emigrating, and by a foreign citizen inheriting a PRC estate, is governed by the separate provisional rules on sale and payment of foreign exchange for outward transfer of personal property.

Overseas ATM withdrawals on domestic bank cards are capped at RMB 100,000 equivalent per person per civil year, with a per-card daily ceiling of RMB 10,000 equivalent; exceeding the annual cap blocks overseas cash withdrawal in the current and following year.

For outbound payments relating to services and certain other items, a tax recordal (备案) must be completed before the first payment under a contract; repeat payments under the same contract need no new recordal.

PRC individual income tax rates are 3%-45% progressive for comprehensive income, 5%-35% for business income, and a flat 20% for interest/dividends, asset leasing, asset transfers and incidental income.
The US-PRC treaty caps PRC tax on dividends, interest and royalties paid to a US beneficial owner at 10% of the gross amount.

Converting RMB to virtual currency inside China is prohibited: virtual-currency business activity is classified as illegal financial activity, and financial institutions may not provide account, transfer or settlement services for it.

US taxpayers must express foreign-currency amounts in USD, generally at the spot rate when the item is received, paid or accrued; the IRS has no official rate and generally accepts any posted rate used consistently. The 2025 yearly average for China was 7.129 CNY/USD.

Section 988 does not apply to an individual's personal transaction; where nonfunctional currency is disposed of in a personal transaction, no gain is recognised by reason of exchange-rate changes unless the gain would exceed USD 200.

A US credit for PRC tax is claimed on Form 1116, is limited by the US tax on foreign-source income, may be carried back one year and forward ten, and is not available for income excluded under the foreign earned income exclusion; only tax at the treaty-capped rate qualifies.
locator: S15 body; S16 'Foreign Tax Credit limit'

statement: Form 8938 thresholds are USD 50,000 year-end / 75,000 any-time for an unmarried taxpayer living in the US, and USD 200,000 / 300,000 living abroad; failing to file can cost up to USD 10,000 plus 10,000 per 30 days after notice, capped at USD 60,000. An FBAR is required where foreign accounts exceed USD 10,000 in aggregate at any time in the calendar year.

The current adjusted FBAR civil maxima in the eCFR table are USD 16,536 for a non-willful violation and USD 165,353 for a willful violation; the table was last amended at 90 FR 5630 (17 January 2025) and is headed as applying to penalties assessed on or after that date.
Carrying more than USD 10,000 into or out of the US must be reported to CBP on FinCEN Form 105; the threshold applies to a family or group's combined amount, and failure risks seizure and forfeiture.

HSBC China's tariff effective 31 October 2026 publishes outward telegraphic transfer fees of: Private Banking individual customer free; Premier and Advance 0.1% of the remittance with a CNY 100 minimum and CNY 500 maximum plus a CNY 120 cable charge; Private Banking entity 0.1% with a CNY 100 minimum and CNY 1,000 maximum plus cable. A 'Pay Exact' (OUR) request costs CNY 200 and Premier Elite customers are exempt from the service fee.
The HSBC tariff expressly excludes charges collected by other institutions and any duties, levies, charges or taxes imposed by authorities.

Evasion of FX controls and unauthorised trading in foreign exchange attract fines of up to 30% of the amount, or 30% to an equal amount in serious cases, with criminal liability where constituted.

Failure to file required foreign-trust information carries a penalty of the greater of USD 10,000 or 35% of the gross reportable amount (5% substituted for returns under section 6048(b)), plus USD 10,000 per 30-day period after 90 days from IRS notice, with a reasonable-cause exception.
